text.tspan: Did Sanskrit "evolve" until P
ān
ini "codified" it? Are the Vedas merely "religious
chants"? Did Sanskrit descend from Proto-Indo-European, or do Greek, Latin, and
other Eurasian languages preserve reflections of Sanskrit's outward radiance?
Atomic Sanskrit takes a clear position. It argues that Sanskrit is engineered, that the
Vedas serve as its distributed calibrant, and that Sanskrit's radiant architecture
traveled beyond India.
The Source and Reference Companion makes the evidence behind that argument
available for inspection.
The main book uses concise numbered endnotes so that its argument can proceed
without forcing every reader through the complete apparatus. Each note carries a
stable identifier. The same identifier leads to a full entry in this volume containing
the primary-source passage, complete citation, translation, verification trail, source
history, and an explanation of how the evidence supports the book.
Reference-only appendices preserve the larger datasets, calculations, comparisons,
and technical demonstrations.
The main volume develops the case. The companion allows reviewers, critics,
Sanskrit scholars, and interested readers to examine how that case was built.
Parag Tope comes from Tatya Tope's family lineage and is the author of Tatya
Tope's Operation Red Lotus, reviewed by The Hindu as "Revisionism at its best." An
IIT Bombay dropout, mechanical engineer, entrepreneur, and University of Michigan
Ross MBA, his work challenges inherited Western accounts of Indian history and
civilization.
